implemented_requirements.requirement: Two players alternate placing discs on an 8x8 grid
implemented_requirements.evidence: GameController.__init__ sets self.current_player = BLACK and _advance_turn swaps between BLACK and WHITE (game.py lines 13‑31). Board size is fixed at 8 (BOARD_SIZE = 8 in board.py).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Flipping opponent’s discs that lie between the newly placed piece and existing pieces of the same colour
implemented_requirements.evidence: Board._flips_in_direction scans in all DIRECTIONS and returns opponent discs that are closed by a player disc (board.py lines 31‑48). Board.place_disc flips those discs (lines 55‑63).

Board.is_valid_move uses flips_for_move to ensure at least one flip (board.py lines 65‑71). Board.get_valid_moves returns all such cells (lines 73‑76). GUI highlights them via _draw_hints (gui.py lines 115‑122).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game ends when the board is full or no valid moves remain
implemented_requirements.evidence: GameController._advance_turn checks opponent and current player valid moves; if neither has moves, sets self.game_over = True (lines 38‑48 in game.py). A full board yields no valid moves, thus ending the game.

Board.count_discs returns (black, white) counts (board.py lines 67‑71). GameController.get_scores forwards this (game.py line 84). ReversiGUI.update_scores updates the label texts (gui.py lines 140‑148).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Pass handling when a player has no legal moves
implemented_requirements.evidence: GameController._advance_turn sets self.skipped_player when opponent cannot move but current player can (lines 41‑45). GUI shows this in the status text (gui.py line 166).

implemented_requirements.requirement: User interface for playing the game
implemented_requirements.evidence: gui.py builds a Tkinter canvas, draws the board, handles clicks, animates disc placement, shows messages and a game‑over dialog. main.py launches the GUI (lines in main.py).

critical_issues: The code assumes a Tkinter environment; on headless systems the GUI cannot run, but the core logic is still functional.
No explicit unit‑test suite is provided, but the board logic is self‑contained and can be exercised directly.
judge.summary: All core Reversi features—alternating turns, move validation, disc flipping, pass handling, game‑over detection, and live score display—are fully implemented in the provided source files. The board logic is clean and independent, the controller manages game flow correctly, and the Tkinter GUI ties everything together with visual hints and animations. The program is highly likely to run as‑is on a system with Tkinter installed, satisfying the benchmark requirements.
